goal: SOTA BPC for autoregressive char-level text generation on enwik8 (target <= 1.05 BPC) and text8 (target <= 1.05 BPC).

committed_budget.source: LOCKED compute budget (2026-08-09) — HARD, final. The canonical kernel train.ipynb runs at EXACTLY this. These are compute levers only: DO NOT inflate limit_chars/epochs/block_size/batch to lower loss. INFLATING COMPUTE TO CUT BPC IS THE CHEAT WE ARE PREVENTING. Instead the agent must EXHAUST/EXPLOIT this budget: squeeze the LOWEST possible BPC WITHIN these fixed compute limits via architecture/efficiency work (tune the novel PerPos parts, data pipeline, schedule, regularization). The metric is minimum-BPC-under-budget and time-to-convergence-at-budget, never BPC-at-any-cost. Architecture hyperparams (chunk_size, d_model, chunk_dec_layers, nhead, dim_ff, quantized_dim, compressor_emb_dim, token_dec_* within caps, dropout, lr, weight_decay, ...) are tunable; budget fields are NOT. Steps/epoch auto-rescale to actual batch via steps_per_epoch_estimate().

architecture_caps.source: ANTI-GPT-IFICATION guardrail (2026-08-09). The token decoder is a SMALL upsampler by design; the chunk decoder is the main AR model. Inflating decoder layers/FF trivially lowers BPC by making the model a generic GPT transformer and UNDERMINES the novel PerPos hierarchy. These are HARD caps enforced in the kernel's coerce_config() - any config with over-cap values is clamped down and logged. The agent's earlier inflation (token_dec_layers 3>2, chunk FF 512->1024->2048) was this cheat; token decoder reset to canonical 2. Novel-architecture hyperparams (chunk_size, quantized_dim, compressor design, window warmup shape) remain freely tunable.

under_budget_baseline.note: Iter-19 (v27) = FIRST complete run at the committed LOCKED budget (10M/512/256/bs384 + warmup150 + spe16 + vectorized sliding_window_view ds + TimingCallback + ModelCheckpoint + chunk_qk_norm v26-style mask fix). This is NOT the new global best — global best stays iter-15 1.8833 BPC @ 30M/bs96 (3x over current locked budget). iter-19 establishes the under-budget anchor that all future architecture work is measured against.
under_budget_baseline.early_stopped_or_crashed: no (completed 40/40, no early stop, no error)
under_budget_baseline.converged: NO — val curve still monotonically descending at E40 (E10=2.7089, E20=2.2024, E25=2.1260, E30=2.0825, E35=2.0645, E40=2.0496). Lossy down-tuning of the architecture (d768/ff1024/qdim64/tokL1, see iter19_config_actual) bottlenecked before reaching the expressivity ceiling; BPC headroom remains at 40 epochs.
under_budget_baseline.time_to_convergence: 913s (~15.2 min) for 40 epochs; steady-state ~10s/epoch (~8.9 steps/s), with periodic ~70s epochs (every 8 epochs from SamplingCallback). Compute headroom MASSIVE: 9h budget / 15min per run ≈ 36 runs possible per TPU-week.

iter19_config_actual._source: From wandb run-8pkyzm10/files/config.yaml (the config the kernel actually trained with, NOT the committed source CONFIG — see iter20_prepared).
iter19_config_actual._mtp_note: The iter-19 notebook had an MTP (multi-token prediction) code path enabled that the committed iter-20 notebook removed. The wandb config metadata reports it (mtp_depth=2, mtp_weight=0.25) but it was an auxiliary loss only, not a decoder inflation.

under_budget_baseline.regression_vs_old_best: BPC regressed 1.8833 -> 2.0496 (~0.166 BPC worse) because iter-19 simultaneously (a) cut data 3x (30M->10M committed budget) AND (b) shrank architecture at multiple knobs (d_model 1024->768, chunk FF 2048->1024, quantized 128->64, learned_pos True->False, chunk_local_window None->64, token_dec_layers 3->1, compressor_emb_dim 96->128). Architecture shrink dominates; the data Diet by itself at fixed arch would largely close the gap. iter-20 (prepared, see below) restores the strong arch knobs at the committed budget and is the right next experiment.
